facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old woman presented with a lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma
there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
the overlying skin was uninvolved
there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm with relatively hypoechoic, heterogeneous internal echoes
A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size
A 59-year-old woman presented with a lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma
there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
the overlying skin was uninvolved
there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm with relatively hypoechoic, heterogeneous internal echoes
A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast cancer and has now presented with a new lump in the same breast, which has increased in size on follow-up, suggesting a possible recurrence.

The firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle, with a lobulated and well-defined appearance on ultrasonography, could be suggestive of a sarcoma, particularly given the history of radiation therapy.
The patient's history of breast-conserving surgery and radiation therapy increases the risk of fat necrosis, which could present as a firm mass with a lobulated appearance on imaging.
The patient's presentation with a firm mass and a lobulated appearance on ultrasonography could be suggestive of a phyllodes tumor, particularly given the lack of axillary lymph node involvement.

rationales.F01: A lump in the breast is a common presentation for breast cancer recurrence.
rationales.F02: Previous breast cancer and radiation therapy increase the risk of breast cancer recurrence.
rationales.F03: A firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle is concerning for malignancy.
rationales.F07: The ultrasonography findings are suspicious for a malignant tumor.
rationales.F09: An increase in lesion size over time is concerning for malignancy.

frontier_selector.rationale: History of breast-conserving surgery and radiation, combined with a new firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle, supports breast cancer recurrence over other options.
